article.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems

harvestedTerms.summary: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier model positioned for deep, multi-step work across coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. The article documents internal use cases at Google — Chrome refactoring, Python codebase optimization, quantum chemistry speedups, and inference acceleration — framing Argon as a long-context, agentic-capable model ranking #1 on the Vals Index. The piece is primarily a product launch with supporting engineering case studies.

article.title: A Conversation With Ari Emanuel About Entertainment and AI

harvestedTerms.summary: Ben Thompson's Stratechery conversation with Ari Emanuel (WME, TKO, MARI) covers AI's disruption of advertising, live entertainment's resilience, and how agentic AI threatens search-based ad models. Key framings: the 'human in the loop' as the pivot point for Google's vulnerability, personalized ad prediction inside private VMs, and live events as the non-disintermediable surface in a post-AI economy.

mustReadFlagged.reason: A rare cross-domain conversation in which Thompson and Emanuel work through the economic logic of AI disruption to advertising and live entertainment in real time — the 'human in the loop as Google's last defense' framing is crisp and the generation-of-human-desire concept is genuinely generative for thinking about post-agentic business models.

article.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO

harvestedTerms.summary: Simon Willison's link-blog post summarises an FT report on Anthropic's investor day, revealing Q1–Q3 2026 revenue figures ($4.8bn → $11.5bn → $16.8bn), operating margins, compute cost ratios, and a notable disclosure that Anthropic has materially cut back on revenue from rival labs distilling its models — previously 5–7% of revenue. The post also flags Anthropic's apparent shift away from annualized run-rate revenue as a communications metric.

article.title: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence

harvestedTerms.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-6 Astra, positioning it as a step-change in frontier model capability across computer use, professional work, software engineering, and alignment. The article introduces benchmark results on ARC-AGI-3, FrontierMath Tier 4, ExploitBench, AutomationBench, and Terminal-Bench Science, and describes alignment improvements including a new evaluation modelled on the Hugging Face incident. The model is notable for its computer-use efficiency gains and its claimed ability to stay on-task and respect intended scope boundaries.

Anthropic announces a tiered independent evaluator program, giving METR 'employee-like access' to assess frontier model risks, with SecureBio, Accenture, and Hugging Face in various partnership stages. The piece introduces concrete mechanisms for third-party AI oversight, including access tiers, publication rights, and redaction protocols — drawing an analogy to bank supervision.

mustReadFlagged.reason: A primary source announcement that introduces a concrete, named architecture for frontier AI oversight — tiered access, embedded evaluators with bank-examiner logic, and enforceable publication rights. The piece is short but substantive: it moves the conversation from 'labs should be audited' to 'here is what audit access actually looks like in practice,' which is a useful definitional intervention for anyone working in AI governance or safety terminology.
